mainTopic: Whether the הלכה follows רבי יהודה or רבי מאיר on eating חמץ on ערב פסח: challenges from a סתם משנה and רבן גמליאל, the ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא, and רבי's story of the deposited חמץ.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a side discussion about witnesses: רב שימי בר אשי teaches that a 'during sunrise' witness and a 'before sunrise' witness contradict each other, and we do not explain away the conflict. Then רב נחמן quotes רב that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who allows eating חמץ on ערב פסח only through the fourth hour. רבא challenges this twice. First, a סתם משנה seems to follow רבי מאיר, but the גמרא shows that its word 'מותר' fits רבן גמליאל instead. Second, he asks why not rule like רבן גמליאל as a מכריע, and רב נחמן answers that רבן גמליאל has a separate reason of his own. Another answer is that רב relied on a ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא: when the fourteenth falls on שבת, everything, even pure תרומה, is burned on Friday, and food for two meals is eaten until four hours. The חכמים argue with him, and the debate ends with the famous rule that אליהו does not come on ערב שבת; the הלכה is set his way, though רב פפא says that ruling is only about removal. Next comes the story of רבי telling a keeper of someone's חמץ to wait through the fourth hour and sell it in the fifth. After a back-and-forth about suspicion and charity collectors, the story is read as following רבי יהודה. Finally, רב יוסף links רבי's ruling to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on selling a spoiling deposit, and אביי begins a challenge from רבי יוחנן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רב שימי בר אשי's ruling about sunrise witnesses is not obvious
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the 'during sunrise' witness only saw early rays of light, so both witnesses agree. רב שימי בר אשי teaches that we do not say this, and the testimony stays void.
steps.simpleTranslation: [You might have said: the one who said] 'during sunrise' was standing out in the open, and he only saw rays of light. [So really both witnesses mean 'before sunrise.'] He teaches us [that we do not say this].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering 'פשיטא — isn't this obvious?' about רב שימי בר אשי's ruling. It explains the mistaken idea his ruling comes to reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have tried to rescue the testimony. Perhaps the second witness stood in an open area, saw the first glow of dawn, and mistook it for sunrise. רב שימי בר אשי teaches that we do not stretch to explain away the conflict, so the two testimonies stay contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunrise; the moment the sun appears
An open, exposed place
Rays or glimmers of light
He teaches us; the ruling comes to tell us this point

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the 'rays of light' explanation as the conclusion! It is the 'you might have thought' (מהו דתימא) idea that רב שימי בר אשי rejects. The conclusion is that the testimony is void.

phrases.english: [The one who said] 'during sunrise' —
phrases.notes: This picks up the 'you might have thought' (מהו דתימא) line that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: he was standing in an open place,
and it was merely rays of light that he saw.
phrases.notes: So he really saw pre-sunrise light, which would match the first witness.

phrases.english: He teaches us [that we do not say this].
phrases.notes: So the two witnesses still contradict each other, and their testimony doesn't count.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּגִילּוּיָיא הֲוָה קָאֵי וְזַהֲרוּרֵי בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דַּחֲזָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge (on the previous amud) against רב שימי בר אשי's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא — the ruling rejects a plausible but mistaken reconciliation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'during sunrise' witness only saw early rays from an open spot, so both witnesses agree and the testimony stands.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not reconcile the witnesses this way, so the testimony is void.

steps.title: רב rules the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so חמץ may be eaten only through the fourth hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main dispute in the משנה and gives a practical ruling. The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view is stricter: one may eat חמץ only through the fourth hour, and in the fifth hour one may not eat it. This ruling sets the target for the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows [this opinion]

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical question of the whole sugya: until what time on ערב פסח may one eat חמץ.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rav said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. It leaves the witness discussion and returns to the dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: one may eat חמץ only through the fourth hour.

steps.title: רבא asks: why not rule like רבי מאיר, since an unattributed משנה follows him?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן. There is a סתם משנה that follows רבי מאיר, and normally the הלכה follows a סתם משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Let the master say that the הלכה is like רבי מאיר, since the תנא taught us an unattributed משנה that follows his view.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the ruling from step 2. He argues the הלכה should follow רבי מאיר instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: when רבי (the editor of the משנה) records an opinion without a name, it shows that he holds that way, so the הלכה follows it. רבא claims such an unnamed משנה exists for רבי מאיר, which would contradict ruling like רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And let the master say (polite challenge form)
The תנא taught us without naming anyone
Like him; in accordance with his view

steps.confusionAlert: 'סתם' here does not mean 'simply.' It means an unattributed משנה, a ruling stated with no name attached, which usually carries הלכה weight.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
And let the Master say the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir,
since the tanna taught us an unattributed mishna in accordance with him.
phrases.notes: There's a rule: when a disagreement is followed later by an unnamed משנה (מחלוקת ואחר כך סתם הלכה כסתם), the הלכה follows the unnamed one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא מָר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דִּסְתַם לַן תְּנָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סתם משנה normally decides the הלכה. If a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר, ruling like רבי יהודה goes against it.

steps.title: The unattributed משנה: whenever one may eat, one may feed
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the סתם משנה: as long as a person may eat חמץ, he may feed it to his animals. This implies there is no in-between time, which matches רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Any time that one is permitted to eat [חמץ], he may feed [it to animals]!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the actual משנה that backs up his challenge. It is the proof behind step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds there is a middle time, the fifth hour. During it a person may not eat חמץ, but he may still feed it to animals. This משנה ties eating and feeding together with no gap, which fits רבי מאיר only.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted
He feeds [it to animals]

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
The entire time that one is permitted to eat — he may feed!
phrases.notes: So there's no time when you may feed but not eat yourself, and that goes against רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן כׇּל שָׁעָה שֶׁמּוּתָּר לֶאֱכוֹל מַאֲכִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text that step 3's challenge depends on.
steps.raayaObject: That a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'כל שעה שמותר לאכול מאכיל', which allows no gap between eating and feeding.

steps.title: That משנה is not really unattributed, because the word 'permitted' does not fit רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. The word 'מותר' does not fit רבי מאיר, so the משנה must follow a different view (רבן גמליאל). It is therefore not a סתם that supports רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That משנה is not an unattributed ruling [for רבי מאיר], because the word 'permitted' is difficult [according to him].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 4. That משנה cannot be counted as a סתם משנה following רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה followed רבי מאיר, it should simply say 'whenever one eats, he feeds.' The word 'מותר' (permitted) hints that some people are permitted to eat at that time and others are not. That fits רבן גמליאל, who allows a כהן to eat תרומה in the fifth hour while others may no longer eat חולין. Since the משנה follows רבן גמליאל, רב's ruling like רבי יהודה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that משנה)
It is not an unattributed ruling
Because it is difficult

steps.whatToRemember: רב rules like רבי יהודה. רבא tried to prove the הלכה follows רבי מאיר from a סתם משנה. The גמרא answers that this משנה is not a true סתם for רבי מאיר, because its word 'מותר' fits רבן גמליאל instead.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the משנה has no author. It says the משנה does not count as an unattributed ruling for רבי מאיר, because its wording points to רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: That one is not an unattributed mishna,
because the word 'permitted' is difficult.
phrases.notes: For רבי מאיר it should have said 'כל שעה שאוכל מאכיל'. The word 'מותר' hints that it depends on the person, the way רבן גמליאל holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא לָאו סְתָמָא הוּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקַשְׁיָא מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4 and so answers רבא's challenge in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that this משנה is a סתם following רבי מאיר. The general rule that a סתם משנה decides the הלכה stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'מותר' does not fit רבי מאיר's view. It fits רבן גמליאל, so the משנה is not a סתם for רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Why not rule like רבן גמליאל as the decider?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: rule like רבן גמליאל, since he decides between the two opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let the Master say that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, since he is the decider.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new challenge to רב נחמן. Since the משנה turned out to follow רבן גמליאל, why not rule like him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says חמץ may be eaten until five hours, and רבי יהודה says until four. רבן גמליאל says regular food until four and תרומה until five, which looks like a middle position. There is a known rule that the הלכה follows a מכריע, the one who decides between two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: a decider: a תנא whose view settles between two other opinions
and let the Master say

phrases.english: And let the Master say
the halacha follows Rabban Gamliel
since he is the decider
phrases.notes: There's a general rule that the הלכה follows the one who decides between two views.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא מָר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 5's finding that the סתם משנה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling (from רב) that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל seems to be a מכריע between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, and the הלכה follows a מכריע. So רב should have ruled like רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל has his own separate reason
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רבן גמליאל is not a decider. He has an independent reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבן גמליאל is not a decider. He is saying a reason of his own.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא: רבן גמליאל does not count as a מכריע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A true מכריע picks a middle path on the same question the others argue about. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה do not distinguish between תרומה and regular food at all. רבן גמליאל adds a new distinction of his own, so he is a third, separate opinion rather than a compromise.

keyTerms.meaning: a reason of his own, an independent line of thinking
he is not a decider

steps.confusionAlert: Even though רבן גמליאל's numbers fall between the other two (four hours and five hours), that alone does not make him a מכריע. A מכריע must be compromising on the same question, not introducing a new distinction.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Rabban Gamliel is not a decider
he is stating a reason of his own
phrases.notes: He splits תרומה from חולין, something the other two never do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָאו מַכְרִיעַ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the status of the opinion: it is an independent view, not a compromise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל sits between four and five hours, so he is a מכריע and the הלכה should follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל adds his own תרומה/חולין distinction, so the rule about a מכריע does not apply.

steps.title: Another answer: רב followed a specific תנא
steps.stepSummary: A second answer to רבא's original challenge: רב was following a particular תנא who holds four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: רב ruled according to this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another explanation of why רב ruled like רבי יהודה. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer defended רב by saying the סתם משנה is not a real source for רבי מאיר. This answer says something new: רב had a separate source, a ברייתא, that clearly supports four hours.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say: introduces an alternative answer
like this תנא

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rav ruled in accordance with this tanna

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַב דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to רבא's challenge from Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different תנא as the basis of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ruled against a סתם משנה with no source of his own.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was relying on a ברייתא that supports the four-hour view.

steps.title: The ברייתא: ערב פסח on שבת
steps.stepSummary: When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, everything is removed before שבת, and food for two meals is kept to eat until four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: When the fourteenth falls on שבת, one removes everything before שבת. One burns impure, doubtful, and pure תרומה, and leaves over from the pure food for two meals, to eat until four hours. These are the words of רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא, who said it in the name of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that רב relied on. It describes what to do when ערב פסח falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because you cannot burn on שבת, the burning is done on Friday. Only enough pure food for two שבת meals is kept, and it must be eaten until four hours, which matches רבי יהודה. This is the source for רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: impure תרומה, which may not be eaten anyway
'hanging' תרומה whose purity is in doubt
pure תרומה
food for two meals (Friday night and שבת morning)
one removes or destroys the חמץ

steps.whyThisMatters: The words 'עד ארבע שעות' are the proof. This תנא clearly holds the four-hour deadline, giving רב a real source for ruling like רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
The fourteenth that falls on Shabbat
one removes everything before Shabbat
and one burns impure terumah
doubtful, and pure
phrases.notes: Even pure תרומה not needed for שבת is burned.

phrases.english: and one leaves over from the pure
food for two meals
in order to eat until four hours

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ בַּרְתּוֹתָא
phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Elazar ben Yehuda of Bartota
who said it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source promised in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that חמץ is eaten only until four hours
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא in the name of רבי יהושע: 'כדי לאכול עד ארבע שעות'

steps.title: The חכמים object to burning pure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say pure תרומה should not be burned, because a כהן to eat it might still be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Pure תרומה should not be burned. Perhaps people will be found to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, the חכמים argue with רבי אלעזר בן יהודה about one detail: burning pure תרומה on Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Destroying pure תרומה is normally forbidden. Since a כהן might show up on שבת to eat it, burning it on Friday could turn out to be a needless waste of holy food.

keyTerms.meaning: eaters, meaning כהנים who may eat the תרומה
they should not be burned

phrases.english: They said to him:
pure ones should not be burned
perhaps eaters will be found for them

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: טְהוֹרוֹת לֹא יִשָּׂרְפוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues with a dispute over one detail of its ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling to burn pure תרומה before שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן may still turn up to eat it, so burning it now may be needless destruction of תרומה.

steps.title: They already searched for כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that they already looked for כהנים and found none.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They already searched and did not find.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן יהודה replies to the חכמים' objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is one where people already checked the city for כהנים who could eat the תרומה. Since none were found, there is no real chance of an eater appearing, so burning is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: they already searched

phrases.english: He said to them:
They already searched and did not find

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: כְּבָר בִּקְּשׁוּ וְלֹא מָצְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן might still be found, so the תרומה must be kept.
steps.terutzMaskana: A search was already made and no כהן was found.

steps.title: Maybe כהנים slept outside the city wall
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים respond that כהנים might have slept outside the wall and could come in on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Perhaps they slept outside the wall?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A search inside the city does not cover כהנים who spent the night just outside the walls. They could enter on שבת morning and eat the תרומה, so the possibility is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: outside the city wall
they slept, spent the night

phrases.english: They said to him:
Perhaps they slept outside the wall?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שֶׁמָּא חוּץ לַחוֹמָה לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the search settled the matter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The search did not cover people outside the wall, who might still arrive on שבת.

steps.title: Then don't burn doubtful תרומה either
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers back: by your logic, even doubtful תרומה should not be burned, because אליהו might come and declare it pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: According to your words, even doubtful תרומה should not be burned. Perhaps אליהו will come and declare it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר turns the חכמים' reasoning against them to show it goes too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we worry about unlikely events like כהנים sleeping outside the wall, we should also worry that אליהו will come and settle the doubt about the תלויות. But the חכמים agree that תלויות are burned, so their worry must be too far-fetched.

keyTerms.meaning: according to your words, using your own logic
אליהו הנביא, who will clarify doubtful matters in the future
and he will declare them pure

phrases.english: He said to them:
According to your words
even doubtful terumah should not be burned
perhaps Eliyahu will come and declare them pure

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם, אַף תְּלוּיוֹת לֹא יִשָּׂרְפוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rebuts Step 12 by showing its logic would lead to an unacceptable result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' concern for unlikely possibilities
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their logic would also forbid burning תלויות because of the unlikely chance that אליהו comes. Since they do burn תלויות, the logic fails.

steps.title: אליהו does not come on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that ישראל was promised that אליהו will not come on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, because of the bother.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Israel has already been assured that אליהו does not come on ערב שבת or on ערב יום טוב, because of the bother.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי אלעזר's comparison. This closes the back-and-forth in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are different. The chance of אליהו coming on Friday is not just unlikely, it is ruled out by a known promise, because people are busy preparing for שבת. כהנים outside the wall are a real possibility, so the חכמים still say not to burn pure תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: assured, promised
the eves of שבת (Fridays)
the eves of יום טוב
bother, effort, busy preparations

steps.whatToRemember: The main point for our sugya is that this ברייתא says to eat until four hours, giving רב a source for ruling like רבי יהודה. The dispute about burning pure תרומה is a side detail, and it ends with the famous rule that אליהו does not come on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Israel has already been assured
that Eliyahu does not come
not on Shabbat eves
and not on Yom Tov eves
because of the bother
phrases.notes: His coming would pull people away from their holiday preparations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּבָר מוּבְטָח לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the comparison made in Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Worrying about כהנים outside the wall is like worrying about אליהו coming, so both should stop the burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: אליהו is promised not to come on ערב שבת, so there is no worry for תלויות. כהנים outside the wall remain a real possibility.

steps.title: The חכמים rule like רבי אלעזר בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The debate ends. The חכמים did not leave until they set the הלכה like רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא, who spoke in the name of רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: They did not move from there until they set the law like רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא, who said it in the name of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The back-and-forth from Steps 10–14 is over. The ברייתא tells us the final ruling: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא held that on Friday one burns even pure תרומה, keeping only enough for two שבת meals, which are eaten until four hours. The חכמים had objected to burning pure תרומה. This line closes the debate and settles the law his way, against the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not move from there (they stayed until it was decided)
They set the law
A man from the town of Bartota

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling of the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא: when the fourteenth falls on שבת, even pure תרומה is burned on Friday, except food for two meals to be eaten until four hours.

phrases.english: They said: They did not move from there
until they set the law

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ בַּרְתּוֹתָא
phrases.english: like Rabbi Elazar ben Yehuda of Bartota
who said it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: לֹא זָזוּ מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁקָּבְעוּ הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the argument between the חכמים and רבי אלעזר with a final ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא: pure תרומה not needed for the two שבת meals is burned on Friday, and the leftover is eaten until four hours.

steps.title: Does this ruling also cover eating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ruling like רבי אלעזר might also mean the הלכה follows רבי יהודה about eating חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not that the ruling applies even to eating?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to learn something new from the ruling it just quoted. It asks whether this ruling also tells us when one may still eat חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling covers eating, then the הלכה would follow רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה holds that one may eat חמץ only until the end of the fourth hour. That would support רב נחמן's earlier ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not that…? (opens a suggested proof)
To eat

phrases.english: What, is it not
even regarding eating?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, אֲפִילּוּ לֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to draw a wider rule about eating from the ruling in Step 15
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יהודה on eating חמץ (only until the end of the fourth hour)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling like רבי אלעזר בן יהודה איש ברתותא

steps.title: No, the ruling is only about getting rid of it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, quoting רבא, says the ruling is only about removing the תרומה, not about eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: No, it is about removing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes away the proof from Step 16. The ruling was only about when to get rid of the תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling only settles the removal question: when no כהן is available, even pure תרומה is burned before שבת. It does not adopt רבי אלעזר's phrase 'to eat until four hours,' so it cannot prove that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה on eating.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
To remove or get rid of (the חמץ)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
No, it is regarding removal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: לֹא, לְבַעֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in Step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The ruling does not address eating at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof read the ruling as covering eating. It really only covers when to remove the תרומה.

steps.title: רבי and the bag of חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבי also holds like רב נחמן, and brings a story. A man had a bag of someone else's חמץ that mice had chewed open. רבי told him to wait through hours one to four, and in the fifth hour told him to sell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי held like רב נחמן. As רבין בר רב אדא said: There was a story with a man who left a saddlebag full of חמץ with יוחנן חקוקאה. Mice bit holes in it, and the חמץ was spilling out. He came before רבי. In the first hour רבי said to him: Wait. In the second, he said: Wait. In the third, he said: Wait. In the fourth, he said: Wait. In the fifth, he said: Go and sell it in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings new support for רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. The support is a story about רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through hours one to four, רבי kept saying wait, because the owner might still return and eat his חמץ. In the fifth hour רבי said to sell it. That suggests the חמץ could no longer be eaten by its owner at that point, which would fit רבי יהודה. The next step spells out this inference.

keyTerms.meaning: And even רבי holds this view
A saddlebag or sack
Deposited (left it for safekeeping)
Spilling or poking out
Wait

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. He is not the same person as the תנא רבי יהודה (בר אילעאי), whose view on eating חמץ is being tested.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבִּי סָבַר לְהָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן.
phrases.english: And even Rebbi holds like this view of Rav Nachman.
As Ravin bar Rav Adda said:
There was a story with a certain man
who left a saddlebag full of chametz
with Yochanan Chakuka'a,
and mice bit holes in it,
and the chametz was spilling out.
And he came before Rebbi.
In the first hour, he said to him: Wait.
In the second, he said to him: Wait.
In the third, he said to him: Wait.
In the fourth, he said to him: Wait.
In the fifth, he said to him:
Go and sell it in the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי סָבַר לְהָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, brings a different source to support רב נחמן
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story told by רבין בר רב אדא about רבי and the bag of חמץ

steps.title: Selling to non-Jews fits רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. Selling in the fifth hour must mean selling to non-Jews, because a Jew may no longer eat it, as רבי יהודה says.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not that he meant to sell it to non-Jews, like רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the story supports רבי יהודה. It reads 'sell it' as 'sell it to non-Jews.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, a Jew may not eat חמץ in the fifth hour, but may still get benefit from it, such as by selling it. So רבי waited until the end of the fourth hour, while eating was still allowed. Then he said to sell it to non-Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: To non-Jews

phrases.english: What, is it not to non-Jews —
like Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, לְגוֹיִם כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the story in Step 18 proves the point
steps.raayaObject: That רבי holds like רבי יהודה: no eating חמץ in the fifth hour
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's instruction in the fifth hour to sell the חמץ, understood as selling to non-Jews

steps.title: Maybe he meant selling to Jews, like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the proof. Maybe רבי meant selling to Jews, who may still eat חמץ in the fifth hour according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: No, he meant to sell it to Jews, like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a different reading of the story, so it no longer proves anything about רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a Jew may eat חמץ until the end of the fifth hour. In that case, רבי was telling him to sell quickly to a Jew before the sixth hour, when it becomes forbidden. Since the story fits רבי מאיר too, it does not prove רבי held like רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: To a Jew
Like רבי מאיר (one may eat חמץ through the fifth hour)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: No,
to a Jew — like Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָא, לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in Step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof. The story can fit רבי מאיר just as well.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the buyers were non-Jews. They could have been Jews.

steps.title: If a Jew may eat it, let him take it himself
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. If a Jew may still eat the חמץ, why sell it? The keeper could just take it for himself and pay the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If it is for a Jew, let him take it for himself!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's reading from Step 20. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Jews may still eat it, telling him to go sell it in the market seems pointless. The keeper himself is a Jew. He could simply take the חמץ and pay the owner back later. So the instruction to 'sell it' seems to point to non-Jews after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him take it for himself

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If it is to a Jew —
let him take it for himself!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִישְׁקְלֵיהּ לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's rejection in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading that רבי meant selling to Jews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If Jews may still eat it, there is no reason to send the keeper to the market. He could take it himself. So the instruction to sell suggests the buyers were non-Jews.

steps.title: The keeper may not buy it himself because of suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers אביי. The keeper must sell the חמץ to others and not keep it for himself, because people might suspect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of suspicion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's question from step 21 in just two words: the keeper doesn't take the חמץ for himself because people might suspect him of wrongdoing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי asked why רבי said 'sell it' if the keeper could simply keep it and pay. The answer is that if the keeper buys it himself, onlookers may think he paid too little or took it for free. Selling it to outsiders keeps him above suspicion. This saves רב יוסף's reading that the sale was to Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspicion, meaning that people might wrongly think someone acted dishonestly

phrases.english: Because of suspicion.
phrases.notes: This is the complete answer to אביי's question.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם חֲשָׁדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces an outside concern (avoiding suspicion) that explains why the keeper sells instead of buying.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a Jew may eat the חמץ, the keeper should just take it himself and pay the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must sell it to others so that no one suspects him of cheating the owner.

steps.title: Charity collectors must sell to others, not to themselves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the idea of avoiding suspicion. Charity collectors who have no poor people to give to must exchange coins or sell food with other people, not with themselves, because of the פסוק 'והייתם נקיים מה׳ ומישראל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Charity collectors who have no poor people to give the money to may exchange the coins with other people, but not with themselves. Collectors of food for the charity plate who have no poor people to give the food to may sell it to other people, but not to themselves. This is because the פסוק says: 'And you shall be clean before ה׳ and before Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that a person handling someone else's goods should deal with outsiders, so no one suspects him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins and food held for the poor can be lost: coins may lose value or rot, and food spoils. So the collectors may exchange or sell them. They must not do the deal with themselves, because people could suspect they gave themselves a good price. The פסוק teaches that being honest before ה׳ is not enough. A person must also look honest to other people.

keyTerms.meaning: Charity collectors who gather money for the poor
Exchange coins, for example trading small coins for larger ones so they don't spoil
Collectors of food for the community charity plate, given out daily to the poor
'You shall be clean before ה׳ and before Israel.' One must look honest to people too.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the rule that a person must avoid even the appearance of wrongdoing, a principle used widely in הלכה.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: charity collectors
who have no poor people to distribute to
exchange the coins with others
phrases.notes: For example, they trade copper coins, which can rust, for silver ones.

phrases.english: but do not exchange them with themselves.
Collectors for the charity plate,
who have no poor people to distribute to
sell the food to others
but do not sell it to themselves,
because it says:
'And you shall be clean before ה׳ and before Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a source for the 'suspicion' answer given in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that someone holding another's property must sell it to outsiders to avoid suspicion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about charity collectors, based on the פסוק 'והייתם נקיים מה׳ ומישראל.'

steps.title: רב אדא בר מתנה reminds רב יוסף of his own earlier teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה tells רב יוסף that he once taught them clearly that רבי meant 'sell it to non-Jews,' following רבי יהודה. This cancels רב יוסף's rejection in step 20.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said to רב יוסף: You told us clearly that רבי said 'Go and sell it to non-Jews,' following רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף's student reminds him that he himself used to teach the story with the words 'sell it to non-Jews.' That reading follows רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, רב יוסף suggested that רבי meant selling to Jews, which would follow רבי מאיר. But רב יוסף's own earlier teaching stated outright that the sale was to non-Jews. That fits only רבי יהודה, who holds that Jews may not eat חמץ in the fifth hour. So the original proof that רבי agrees with רב נחמן's view stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, clearly
Non-Jews

steps.confusionAlert: Why would רב יוסף forget his own teaching? The גמרא elsewhere (נדרים מ״א) tells that רב יוסף became ill and forgot his learning. His students often reminded him of things he had taught them before.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to Rav Yosef:
You told us explicitly
'Go and sell them to non-Jews,'
following Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְרַב יוֹסֵף: בְּפֵירוּשׁ אֲמַרְתְּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns רב יוסף's rejection (step 20) and brings back the proof from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's suggestion that רבי meant selling to Jews.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף's own earlier teaching stated explicitly that the sale was to non-Jews, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי's ruling follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains which תנא רבי's ruling follows. A keeper selling a deposit to prevent loss matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says spoiling deposited produce is sold in court because of השבת אבידה. The תנא קמא says not to touch it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose view does this teaching of רבי follow? It follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. As we learned in a משנה: If someone deposits produce with a friend, even if the produce is going to ruin, the friend should not touch it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He should sell it through the court, because of the מצוה of returning lost property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף opens a new point. He asks which תנא would agree with רבי's ruling that the keeper should sell the owner's חמץ. He answers that it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and quotes the משנה about produce deposited with someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the משנה says that a keeper must not touch a deposit, even if it is spoiling, because the owner may want his own produce back. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the keeper should sell it through בית דין, because saving the owner's money is part of השבת אבידה. רבי telling the keeper to sell the חמץ fits only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
One who deposits an item with someone else for safekeeping
Being ruined or lost, for example produce rotting or eaten by bugs
Court. The sale is done through the court to protect everyone.
The מצוה of returning lost property, which includes preventing a loss

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's ruling to sell the deposited חמץ follows רבי יהודה on the time limit (non-Jews only in the fifth hour). It also follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on selling a deposit to prevent loss.
steps.whyThisMatters: It connects the חמץ story to a wider halachic debate in דיני פקדון: may a keeper sell a deposit to save its value, or must he leave it untouched?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
In accordance with whom does it go,
this teaching of Rabbi?
In accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
as we learned in a mishna:
One who deposits produce with his friend,
even if they are being ruined,
he should not touch them.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He sells them through the court
because of the מצוה of returning lost property.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the fifth-hour question is settled, רב יוסף moves to a different part of רבי's ruling: the keeper's permission to sell a deposit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's instruction to sell the deposited חמץ follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who requires selling a spoiling deposit in court because of השבת אבידה. The תנא קמא forbids touching it.

steps.title: אביי begins quoting רבי יוחנן to limit the dispute
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף by citing a known teaching. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that the תנא קמא's ruling ('don't touch it') applies only in a limited case. The quote is cut off at 'לא שנו אלא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But wasn't it said about that משנה, רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this when...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to challenge רב יוסף's claim from step 25 by quoting a teaching of רבי יוחנן about that very משנה. This line sets up the challenge, and the actual limiting condition comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said that only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows selling a spoiling deposit. אביי is about to show that רבי יוחנן narrowed the תנא קמא's 'don't touch it' to a limited situation. If that is true, the תנא קמא might also allow selling in a case of serious loss, and then רבי's ruling would not have to follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל alone.

keyTerms.meaning: "But wasn't it stated about it?" A rhetorical opening that brings in a known teaching in order to challenge someone.
"They only taught this when..." A formula that limits a ruling to a narrower case.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished on this amud. Do not decide yet what רבי יוחנן limited. The condition after 'לא שנו אלא' is the whole point of the challenge, and it comes next.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: אביי is speaking to רב יוסף, responding to step 25.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it,
phrases.notes: 'It' refers to the משנה about spoiling deposited produce.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
phrases.notes: The person passing on the teaching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: The original source of the teaching.

phrases.english: They only taught this when...
phrases.notes: This limits the תנא קמא's ruling. The condition continues on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מימרא (it quotes an אמורא's statement, but its function is to challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְלָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's claim in step 25 that רבי's ruling follows only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and not the תנא קמא, allows selling a spoiling deposit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן limited the תנא קמא's 'don't touch it' ruling to a narrower case. That suggests the תנא קמא might also allow selling in a case of serious loss. If so, רבי's ruling could fit both views, and not only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
